points: The B-complex vitamins are water-soluble, so any excess is excreted in urine.
Most B-complex vitamins are not stored in the body in useful amounts, so they must be supplied daily in the diet.
The B-complex vitamins act mainly as coenzymes, helping enzymes release energy from carbohydrate, fat and protein.
Wholegrain cereals, meat, pulses and fortified breakfast cereals are the main dietary sources of the B-complex group.

notes.h: Vitamin B1 (thiamine): sources, functions and deficiency
points: Thiamine sources include wholegrain cereals, pork, pulses, nuts and fortified breakfast cereals.
Thiamine acts as a coenzyme that helps release energy from carbohydrate.
Thiamine is needed for normal nerve function and for a healthy heart.
Beriberi is the deficiency disease, with fatigue, weakness, depression, irritability and memory loss.
Dry beriberi damages the nerves, causing numbness and weakness; wet beriberi affects the heart.
Heavy alcohol use reduces the absorption of thiamine, which can lead to deficiency.

notes.h: Vitamin B2 (riboflavin): sources, functions and deficiency
points: Riboflavin sources include milk and dairy products, eggs, lean meat, liver, green vegetables, mushrooms and fortified cereals.
Riboflavin helps release energy from carbohydrate, fat and protein.
Riboflavin helps maintain healthy skin, eyes and mucous membranes.
A deficiency causes cracks and soreness at the corners of the mouth, known as angular cheilitis.
A deficiency also causes a sore, inflamed tongue, skin disorders and eyes that are sensitive to light.

notes.h: Niacin (vitamin B3): sources, functions and deficiency
points: Niacin sources include meat, poultry, fish, peanuts, wholegrain cereals, mushrooms, eggs, milk and fortified cereals.
The body can make niacin from the amino acid tryptophan, found in protein foods.
Niacin helps release energy from carbohydrate, fat and protein.
Niacin keeps the skin, nervous system and digestive system healthy.
Deficiency causes pellagra, with the four Ds: dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia and death.

notes.h: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine): sources, functions and deficiency
points: Pyridoxine sources include chicken, fish such as tuna and salmon, pork, potatoes, bananas, pulses, wholegrain cereals and nuts.
Pyridoxine is needed for the breakdown and use of amino acids, so it is central to protein metabolism.
Pyridoxine helps the body form haemoglobin in red blood cells.
Pyridoxine takes part in making neurotransmitters, the chemicals that carry messages between nerve cells.
Deficiency causes skin rashes around the mouth and nose, confusion, depression and anaemia.

notes.h: The other B-group vitamins: properties (Higher Level only)
points: Thiamine is destroyed by alkalis and by prolonged heat, and it is lost into cooking water.
Riboflavin is destroyed by light, which is why milk in clear bottles loses riboflavin.
Riboflavin is heat-stable in normal cooking and gives a yellow colour to solutions that contain it.
Niacin is stable to heat, light and air, so little is lost in normal cooking.
Niacin is soluble in water and can be lost into cooking water if it is boiled and drained.
Pyridoxine is sensitive to light and is lost into cooking water.

keyTerms.definition: A non-protein helper molecule, often derived from a B-group vitamin, that allows an enzyme to carry out its reaction.
Vitamin B1, a water-soluble vitamin that helps release energy from carbohydrate and supports nerve function.
The deficiency disease caused by a lack of thiamine, with fatigue, weakness, nerve damage and heart problems.
Vitamin B2, a water-soluble vitamin that helps release energy and keeps the skin, eyes and mucous membranes healthy.
Cracking and soreness at the corners of the mouth, caused by a lack of riboflavin.
Vitamin B3, which the body can make from tryptophan and which helps release energy from food.
The deficiency disease caused by a lack of niacin, with dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia and death.
Vitamin B6, needed for the breakdown of amino acids and the formation of haemoglobin.
An essential amino acid from protein foods that the body can convert into niacin.
A chemical that carries nerve impulses across the gap between two nerve cells.

factCards.term: The four Ds of niacin deficiency

factCards.definition: Fatigue, weakness, depression and irritability, memory loss, and nerve or heart damage.

factCards.term: Mouth and tongue signs of low riboflavin intake
factCards.definition: Cracks at the corners of the mouth, a sore inflamed tongue, and eyes sensitive to light.

factCards.term: Three roles shared by the B-group vitamins
factCards.definition: Acting as coenzymes; releasing energy from carbohydrate, fat and protein; maintaining a healthy nervous system.

factCards.term: Two roles of pyridoxine in the body
factCards.definition: Breaking down and using amino acids; helping to form haemoglobin.

questions.prompt: Name two B-group vitamins and state the deficiency disease caused by a lack of each.
questions.model: Any two correctly matched pairs: thiamine (B1) causes beriberi; niacin (B3) causes pellagra; riboflavin (B2) causes cracks at the corners of the mouth and a sore tongue; pyridoxine (B6) causes skin rashes, confusion, depression and anaemia. One mark for each correct vitamin and one for each correct disease or effect.

questions.prompt: Discuss the role of the B-complex vitamins in releasing energy from food, giving the sources and the effects of deficiency for at least two named vitamins.
questions.model: B-complex vitamins are water-soluble and act mainly as coenzymes in energy metabolism; they are not stored in useful amounts so a daily dietary supply is needed. Thiamine (B1): wholegrain cereals, pork, pulses, nuts; releases energy from carbohydrate; deficiency causes beriberi with fatigue, weakness, memory loss and nerve or heart damage. Riboflavin (B2): milk, eggs, lean meat, liver, green vegetables, mushrooms; helps release energy from carbohydrate, fat and protein; deficiency causes angular cheilitis, a sore tongue and light-sensitive eyes. Niacin (B3): meat, poultry, fish, peanuts, wholegrain cereals, eggs; can be made from tryptophan; releases energy from carbohydrate, fat and protein; deficiency causes pellagra with dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia and death. Pyridoxine (B6): chicken, fish, pork, potatoes, bananas, pulses; needed for amino acid metabolism; deficiency causes skin rashes, confusion, depression and anaemia. Losses: thiamine and pyridoxine are lost into cooking water; riboflavin is destroyed by light.
